entries.text: Integrating Knowledge and Skills Through Experience is satisfied through co-op.

Students can choose to complete one or two six-month co-op experiences, or none at all, during their course of study. Students must consult with their advisor regarding the 1-semester-hour prerequisite course for co-op.

A grade of C or higher is required for public health core courses, science requirement courses, and HSCI and PHTH capstone courses. Students who take College: An Introduction ( HSCI 1000 ) and Professional Development for Bouvé Co-op ( HSCI 2000 ) must achieve a C or higher.

overview_text: The combined major in health science and criminal justice offers students an opportunity to integrate the study of healthcare with relevant topics from criminal justice. Students complete core courses in health sciences and criminal justice and electives focusing on the issues pertinent to factors impacting crime and health, healthcare, and the criminal justice system. The degree is designed to prepare students for a range of careers, including roles in health services management, policy analyses, policy development, as well as serving as the foundation for future careers.
